p: The Abgaal belong to the Mudulood, one of the divisions of the Hiraab, with the Habar Gidir, Sheekhaal and Duduble. The clan is regarded as relatively young, its founder dating from the 1500s. A tradition recorded by the Italian scholar Enrico Cerulli makes the founder, Ali Isman, the son of Osman Darandolle of the Hiraab and of Faduma Sarjeele, a woman of the Gareen house that headed the Ajuran Sultanate.

According to the story, Faduma's father was warned that the boy's descendants would drive out his own and tried to poison him, but the mother drank the poison by mistake. The boy hid behind a camel and called the camels his grandfather, whence the name Abgaal, camel-grandfather. Cerulli read the story as a memory of fighting between Abgaal pastoral nomads coming from the north and the Ajuran.

Clan traditions say that the Abgaal Darandoolle began to arrive in the hinterland of Mogadishu in the sixteenth century, while the Muzaffar dynasty ruled the town, and manuscripts from Mogadishu record Abgaal nomads in the interior at about the same time. Towards the end of the seventeenth century an imam of Abgaal descent settled in the Shangaani quarter. His lineage, the Yaaquub, intermarried with merchant families of Yemeni origin and became known in the trade between the coast and the interior, and by the 1700s it ruled most of the town.

Traditions of the fall of the Ajuran speak of heavy taxes and of a quarrel over watering rights, after which the Darandoolle killed the Ajuran imam at a well called Ceel Cawl. According to oral tradition as reported by Lee Cassanelli, the Hiraab Imamate that followed was an alliance of related groups that ruled from the Shabelle valley to the arid lands of Mudug for at least two centuries. Mogadishu was its capital, and the port of Hobyo its commercial centre.

The Abgaal are divided into three main branches: the Harti, the eldest, the Wacbudhan and the Waceysle, the youngest. The imam of the Mudulood and of the Hiraab traditionally comes from the Abgaal, from the Owbakar sub-clan, while the ugaas of the Mudulood comes from the Reer Ugaas sub-clan. Mogadishu is regarded as Abgaal territory, and they form the majority of its population. Three presidents of Somalia, Ali Mahdi Muhammad, Sharif Sheikh Ahmed and Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, have been Abgaal, as was Daud Abdulle Hirsi, the first commander-in-chief of the Somali National Army.

notes: The history rests on oral traditions quoted at length in the article (Cerulli, Cassanelli); I have said so each time. The article itself states flatly that the Ajuran 'neglected the sharia law'; I kept only the taxes and the watering quarrel, as tradition.
The article lists the 13th-century saint Sheikh Hussein of Bale as Abgaal although it dates the clan's founder to the 1500s; left out.
The article names a present imam (Mohamed Yusuf) and a present mayor; left out as likely to date.
